text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Thursday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The St. Petersburg tax police froze the correspondent accounts of Snoras, Siauliai, Tauras and Lithuanian Business banks for non-payment of turnover tax.
- A French diplomat who was badly beaten last month in a mugging flew to France, escorted by a neurosurgeon.
- Lithuania's trade deficit with Poland in the first half of this year was 413 million litas, compared to 479 million litas for all of last year.
- Lithuania halted diplomatic relations with Bosnia Herzegovina following similar moves by the European Union and the United States.
- Lithuania's Social Democrats are divided over whom to put forward as a candidate in the December presidential elections.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas urged law enforcement institutions to investigate vandalism of a memorial at Vilnius's oldest Jewish cemetery and to protect Jewish heritage.
- Two students at the state military academy have been detained as suspects in a stone throwing incident involving a diplomat from Kazakhstan.
- The head of the state security department reprimanded the leader of the Lithuanian National Socialist Union Alliance for publishing racist literature.
- Carpet manufacturer Kilimai has distributed its two million litas share issue and its share capital now stands at 5.7 million litas.
- Vilnius ranks 132 in the world's cities in terms cost of living, along with Cleveland and Karachi.

- Experts say the freezing of correspondent accounts of Lithuanian, Latvian and Estonian banks by St. Petersburg tax police is not a political game but is aimed at making sure these accounts are not used to launder money.

- The government decided to increase the share capital of Savings Bank by 20 million litas only through a share issue, rather than a combination of a revaluing of long-term assets and a 14 million litas share issue.
- Polish Economy Minister Wieslaw Kaczmarek said he supported a Lithuanian proposal to join the Polish and Lithaunian energy systems, which would then be linked to the European Union system.
